1.modern-en: Katherina is named as Baptista's elder, sharp-tongued daughter whom no suitor will touch, and made the obstacle to Bianca's match.

3.modern-en: Katherina drags her bound sister Bianca onstage, accepts Petruchio's wooing under protest, and is announced betrothed before she can prevent it.

5.modern-en: Katherina waits in vain for Petruchio on her wedding day, is humiliated by his late, ragged arrival, and is dragged off without the wedding feast.

6.modern-en: Katherina arrives starving and exhausted at Petruchio's country house and watches him refuse her food and a bed under the pretext of high standards.

8.modern-en: Katherina is denied a new gown by Petruchio, who picks a fight with the tailor and pretends nothing he sees is good enough for her.

10.modern-en: On the road back to Padua, Katherina agrees with Petruchio that the sun is the moon, accepting the absurdity in order to be allowed to proceed.

11.modern-en: Katherina greets old Vincentio in the street as Petruchio names him and plays along with each turn of the joke.

12.modern-en: Katherina answers Petruchio's summons before the other wives and delivers the long final speech on a wife's duty to her husband.

epithet.en: A gentleman of Verona, Katherina's husband

2.modern-en: Petruchio arrives in Padua looking for a rich wife, hears Hortensio describe the dowried but ungovernable Katherina, and declares she will do.

3.modern-en: Petruchio negotiates Katherina's dowry with Baptista in advance, then woos Katherina by ignoring everything she says and announcing they are betrothed.

5.modern-en: Petruchio shows up to his wedding scandalously late, in shabby clothes, and on a broken horse, then hauls Katherina away before the wedding meal.

6.modern-en: Petruchio brings Katherina home, abuses the servants, sends back the meal as unworthy, and lays out his plan to tame her by depriving her of food and sleep.

8.modern-en: Petruchio rages at the haberdasher and tailor about Katherina's new clothes, sending all the finery away as inadequate.

9.modern-en: Petruchio is referred to in Padua as the husband who has whisked Kate off to his country house.

10.modern-en: Petruchio insists on the road that the sun is the moon, and rewards Katherina the moment she agrees with him.

11.modern-en: Petruchio enjoys the comedy of the rival Vincentios and watches the disguises peel off in front of Baptista.

12.modern-en: Petruchio proposes the wager on the three wives, wins it when Katherina is the only one who comes, and asks her for the lecture.

epithet.en: Baptista's younger daughter, courted by every suitor in Padua

1.modern-en: Bianca is presented in the street as the gentle, sought-after younger sister whose suitors must wait until Katherina is married.

3.modern-en: Bianca is dragged onstage tied up by Katherina and questioned about which suitor she prefers before her father arrives to break up the scene.

4.modern-en: Bianca receives Lucentio and Hortensio as her tutors and quickly works out that one of them is courting her under the lessons.

5.modern-en: Bianca attends Katherina's chaotic wedding and witnesses Petruchio's outrageous performance.

12.modern-en: Bianca refuses to come at Lucentio's summons in the wager and is rebuked from the floor.

epithet.en: A young Pisan in love with Bianca

1.modern-en: Lucentio arrives in Padua, falls in love with Bianca at first sight, and plans to disguise himself as her tutor while Tranio takes his place.

3.modern-en: Lucentio is presented to Baptista as the Latin tutor 'Cambio' and is given private access to Bianca for lessons.

4.modern-en: Lucentio teaches Bianca a Latin lesson in which the construing of the text is in fact his confession of love.

5.modern-en: Lucentio is at Katherina's wedding observing Petruchio's antics.

9.modern-en: Lucentio asks an old traveller to pose as his father Vincentio so that the marriage settlement with Baptista can be signed.

11.modern-en: Lucentio is exposed when the real Vincentio arrives and is forced to confess to Baptista that he has secretly married Bianca.

12.modern-en: Lucentio joins the wager confident Bianca will obey, and loses both the bet and his dignity in the same scene.

epithet.en: A wealthy Paduan gentleman, father of Katherina and Bianca

1.modern-en: Baptista announces in the public street that Bianca may not marry until Katherina is wed, and accepts the two new 'tutors' offered for his younger daughter.

3.modern-en: Baptista hands Katherina over to Petruchio after a single afternoon of wooing, glad to be rid of the problem of her.

5.modern-en: Baptista is mortified by Petruchio's wedding-day behaviour and offers him a calm meal he refuses to stay for.

9.modern-en: Baptista is presented with the false 'Vincentio' to sign the marriage contract for Bianca with Tranio-as-Lucentio.

11.modern-en: Baptista watches in confusion as the real Vincentio arrives and the layers of disguise come apart.

12.modern-en: Baptista is at the wedding feast and witnesses his elder daughter, of all people, win Petruchio's wager.

epithet.en: Petruchio's friend and one of Bianca's suitors

2.modern-en: Hortensio receives Petruchio at his door, tells him about Katherina, and asks him to introduce 'Licio' the music tutor into Baptista's house.

3.modern-en: Hortensio appears at Baptista's with a lute broken over his head by Katherina, then is admitted as Bianca's music tutor.

4.modern-en: Hortensio competes with the disguised Lucentio for time with Bianca and pretends to teach the gamut.

6.modern-en: Hortensio visits Petruchio's country house and watches him work on Katherina in real time.

8.modern-en: Hortensio watches Petruchio drive away the haberdasher and tailor and reports it back to the women.

10.modern-en: Hortensio rides back to Padua with Petruchio and Katherina and witnesses the sun-and-moon game.

11.modern-en: Hortensio gives up on Bianca after seeing her with the disguised Lucentio and turns his attention to a wealthy widow.

12.modern-en: Hortensio loses the wager on the widow and is gently mocked at the wedding feast.

epithet.en: Lucentio's servant, disguised as his master

1.modern-en: Tranio is told by Lucentio to take his place as the young gentleman of Pisa while Lucentio courts Bianca as a tutor.

2.modern-en: Tranio is mentioned in Hortensio and Petruchio's plans for Bianca's suitors.

3.modern-en: Tranio, posing as Lucentio, presents himself to Baptista as a rival suitor for Bianca and begins outbidding Gremio in property.

5.modern-en: Tranio is at Katherina's wedding playing the role of Lucentio to perfection.

7.modern-en: Tranio enlists a passing merchant to pose as the absent Vincentio and confirm the marriage settlement.

9.modern-en: Tranio brings the false Vincentio before Baptista to sign the deal that will let the real Lucentio marry Bianca.

11.modern-en: Tranio is caught out when the real Vincentio arrives and the imposture collapses.

12.modern-en: Tranio is restored to his servant's place and is at the wedding banquet with the rest.
